# #0028 The model that authored the independent eval corpus has been WITHDRAWN: stealth/ox-alpha now returns HTTP 404 identifying itself as ZAI GLM-5.3 Flash, so the batch can never be regenerated by anyone

- 2026-08-26T16:37:07Z `issue`: The model that authored the independent eval corpus has been WITHDRAWN: stealth/ox-alpha now returns HTTP 404 identifying itself as ZAI GLM-5.3 Flash, so the batch can never be regenerated by anyone [src/eval/llm-generate.ts]
- 2026-08-26T16:37:21Z `fix`: #0028 HANDLED, and it vindicates a design decision made at #0026. Found by running the one live mapping call by hand rather than trusting a subagent's stub: OpenRouter returns 404 'Thank you for participating in the Stealth Ox Alpha testing period. This model was ZAI's GLM-5.3 Flash.' This is EXACTLY the risk logged at #0017 — 'cloaked/stealth slugs get renamed or withdrawn with little notice, and the deadline is ~5 Sept' — and the mitigation recorded there (provider-agnostic client, model id from env) made it a one-variable change. Forward-looking defaults swapped to z-ai/glm-5.3-flash in src/eval/llm-generate.ts, web/lib/openrouter.ts, .env.example, web/.env.example; verified live against a Shopify-style header, which mapped all five columns correctly and passed the response parser. DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: fixtures/eval/llm-manifest.json still records model 'stealth/ox-alpha'. That field is a PROVENANCE record of what actually authored those 41 transcripts, not a config value, and rewriting it to a model that did not author them would falsify the audit trail. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE README, and it is a point in the project's favour rather than against it: the independent batch is now UNREPRODUCIBLE — its author no longer exists as an addressable model — yet every number in the report still reproduces offline from a clone with no key, because #0026 split eval:generate:llm (one live call, writes a committed fixture) from eval:generate (reads the fixture, never calls out). Had the generator called the API inline, this withdrawal would have destroyed the eval outright. Worth stating in the README as the reason the committed fixture exists. A future batch from the successor model would be a DIFFERENT author and must be labelled as such, never merged into the existing origin:'llm' group. [src/eval/llm-generate.ts]
